paper.title: Efficient Implementation of Monte Carlo Algorithms on Graphical Processing Units for Simulation of Adsorption in Porous Materials

en.sourceStatus: The official repository, MIT license, and formal paper have all been verified.
en.description: GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo software implemented in CUDA/C++ and SYCL/C++ for simulating molecular adsorption in porous materials (explicitly including MOFs).
en.license: MIT License (code)
en.maintenanceStatus: The official GitHub repository has versioned releases; check the release page for the currently supported hardware paths.
en.mofApplicability: Directly applicable. The official README and the original paper both state that the target materials include MOFs, illustrated with a CO₂ adsorption example in Mg-MOF-74.

problemsSolved: Moves Monte Carlo adsorption simulation of porous materials to GPUs to support high-throughput screening.
Supports adsorption calculations such as mixtures, Widom, and GC-TMMC, not only single-component isotherms.
keyFeatures: NVT, GCMC, NVT-Gibbs, Widom, GC-TMMC
CUDA, ROCm/HIP, and SYCL paths are each supported as stated in the documentation
Can be coupled to machine-learning potentials; this capability does not mean training data are provided
en.trainingUse: Not a training database. ML potentials can be integrated into simulations, but no MOF property data directly usable as an ML training set are provided.
caveats: Compatibility differs among GPU backends and ML potential paths; consult the official documentation before building.
The file contents of the paper SI have been identified from the publisher page; actual download and reuse are subject to the publisher terms.

paper.title: QUANTUM ESPRESSO: a modular and open-source software project for quantum simulations of materials

en.sourceStatus: The official QEF GitLab, GPL license, releases, and MOF application literature have all been verified.
en.description: Open-source periodic DFT platform based on plane waves and pseudopotentials, usable for first-principles workflows on MOFs covering electronic structure, geometry relaxation, vibrations, and reactions.
en.license: GPL-2.0-or-later (code)
en.maintenanceStatus: Official development and releases follow the QEF GitLab; GitHub is a mirror.
en.mofApplicability: Directly applicable to periodic MOF calculations; published studies used Quantum ESPRESSO for structural and electronic property calculations of M-MOF-74.

supplementaryResources.label: Quantum ESPRESSO v7.6
supplementaryResources.dataType: Versioned source archive and release notes

supplementaryResources.label: PWscf input reference
supplementaryResources.dataType: Periodic DFT input and feature documentation

problemsSolved: Provides a computational platform for periodic MOF electronic-structure and magnetism problems that classical force fields cannot describe.
Supports first-principles workflows such as geometry relaxation, vibrations, and reaction paths.
keyFeatures: Plane-wave / pseudopotential DFT
Cell and atomic-position relaxation
DFPT, dispersion corrections, and DFT+U
Extensible to reaction paths and materials property calculations
en.trainingUse: Not a training database. The GPL governs the code and does not license using user-generated calculation results, third-party pseudopotentials, or data from other papers for training.
caveats: MOF results depend on the structure, functional, dispersion, pseudopotential, magnetic state, DFT+U, and convergence settings, and cannot be guaranteed in advance.
The GitHub mirror is not the official entry point for issues or pull requests.

paper.title: Algorithms and tools for high-throughput geometry-based analysis of crystalline porous materials

en.sourceStatus: MOF geometry-analysis capability has been verified; the readable open-source evidence comes from the EPFL LSMO fork.
en.description: C++ tool that analyzes the pore geometry and topology of periodic crystalline porous materials using Voronoi decomposition; usable for MOF pore size, surface area, accessible volume, channel, and open metal site analysis.
en.license: Modified BSD / BSD 3-clause-like (with an additional enhancement clause)
en.maintenanceStatus: Public LSMO fork; the verifiable releases / pushes stop in 2022, and the context differs from the original official release.
en.mofApplicability: Directly applicable. The official website and method paper both list MOFs as target materials and describe open metal site analysis of desolvated MOFs.

supplementaryResources.label: Zeo++-LSMO v0.4.7
supplementaryResources.dataType: C++ source code release archive

problemsSolved: Establishes consistent geometric descriptors and pore-channel connectivity information for large numbers of crystalline porous structures.
Helps screen probe-accessible pores and framework geometry before adsorption / diffusion calculations.
keyFeatures: Largest included sphere and largest free sphere diameters
Accessible surface area, accessible volume, and pore size distribution
Channel dimensionality, blocking spheres, and OMS analysis
MOFs / COFs can be assembled from building blocks and topology files
en.trainingUse: Not a training database; suitable for computing structural descriptors as features for downstream models.
caveats: LSMO v0.4.7 should not be described as the canonical release of the original authors.
The LICENSE cannot be simplified directly to a standard BSD-3-Clause SPDX identifier.
Although the paper mentions Supporting Materials, no directly corresponding attachment URL was confirmed in this verification.

problemsSolved: Provides a successor to RASPA2 that balances speed and readability for force-field simulation of adsorption and diffusion in porous materials.
Computes the density of states and free energies with transition-matrix Monte Carlo, and checks the chemical potential independently through dU/d-lambda of fractional molecules.

The README marks several features (flexible frameworks, reaction ensembles and others) as Experimental; treat them as immature.

capabilities: 逐筆 CIF 取得（免費服務）
zh.license: 專有授權（機構／個人 CSD 授權）；免費 Access Structures 服務有獨立使用條款
zh.maintenanceStatus: 統計頁稱 CSD 超過 140 萬筆精選條目，統計每週產生；具體版本與日期依授權發行。
zh.mofApplicability: 直接相關但非 MOF 專庫。實驗 MOF 結構的主要上游，但本次未核實 CCDC 網站上有可用的 MOF 子集頁面（先前探測的 MOF subset 網址回傳的是首頁式內容，不是 MOF 頁）。

problemsSolved: 提供經過整理與驗證的實驗有機與金屬有機晶體結構，是多數 MOF 結構資料集的原料。
免費服務可取得單一結構，授權服務則支援系統性搜尋與分析。
keyFeatures: 超過 140 萬筆精選條目（CCDC 統計頁）
系統性搜尋與分析經 CSD Portfolio 授權提供
免費逐筆服務須保留 CCDC 與 FIZ Karlsruhe 的標頭與識別碼
含 Python API（授權產品）
zh.trainingUse: 不是開放資料集。免費服務條款禁止系統性下載、再散布與程式化存取；以 CSD 結構建立訓練集須依自身授權條款，並確認是否允許再散布衍生檔。
caveats: 這是授權制商用資料庫，不是開源；本條目列入是因為許多開放 MOF 資料集的上游來源為 CSD。
許多 MOF 資料集（包含本 catalog 的 CoRE MOF 條目）把未修改的 CSD 衍生結構限制在需 CCDC 授權的範圍。
MOSAEC-DB 的 README 稱約 45k 檔因 CSD 授權疑慮未能公開，且其 Zenodo 紀錄已不可取用（HTTP 410）。
本次未核實有 CSD 專屬 MOF 子集的官方頁面，亦未讀取完整授權契約，不應假設特定使用方式被允許。
REFCODE 可能隨 CSD 更新而變動，跨版本的資料集需記錄所用 CSD 版本。
